summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with AML status post double cord blood transplant, was admitted with acute respiratory distress and found to have ARDS. Initial treatment included intubation and broad-spectrum antibiotics, but infectious workup was negative. Imaging and clinical course supported a diagnosis of bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP), leading to initiation of high-dose steroids with gradual taper. He experienced transient facial numbness, likely due to hypotension, with normal neuroimaging. Acute kidney injury, attributed to cyclosporine toxicity, resolved with dose reduction. He developed steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring insulin. Coronary artery disease was identified via CT, with normal stress test but mildly reduced ejection fraction. He was weaned from mechanical ventilation, transitioned to oral prednisone, and discharged to pulmonary rehab on a regimen including immunosuppressants, antifungals, and cardiac medications.
